title: Kristaps Porziņģis stepping away from basketball to deal with health issues - CBS Sports
description: Porziņģis signed a two-year, $40 million deal with the Warriors in free agency this summer
body:
Porziņģis signed a two-year, $40 million deal with the Warriors in free agency this summer
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 6, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:06 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Golden State Warriors big man Kristaps Porzingis announced Friday that he has "made the decision to prioritize my health and step away from the game I love" as he continues to deal with mysterious health issues. It's unclear when, or if, the 31-year-old Porziņģis will return to the court. Porziņģis has not played for the Warriors this season and reports earlier this week indicated that the team is withholding payments from him. He signed a two-year, $40 million deal with the Warriors in free agency this summer, but the second year of the deal only has a $3 million guarantee. Here is Porziņģis' full statement announcing his decision to step away from basketball: This season I was really looking forward to running it with this group, but as I ramped up, my body didn't respond the way I anticipated. I'm doing good, but I know what it takes, and I'm not where I want to be to perform at the level that I expect from myself. At this point, I've made the decision to prioritize my health and step away from the game I love. In this situation, I want to show the utmost respect for the Golden State Warriors and work with them to find a solution that makes sense. I'm thankful to my family and close ones for always being there. Much appreciation to all of you for the support. Porziņģis' career has been defined by health problems. He's played more than 57 games just three times since he was drafted No. 4 overall by the New York Knicks in 2015, and has dealt with significant injuries, including a torn ACL that cost him the entire 2018-19 season. In recent years, he's been limited by this mysterious illness that first became an issue in Boston during the 2024-25 season. Porziņģis started dealing with extreme fatigue and previously disclosed a diagnosis of postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome, or POTS, which is characterized by rapid changes in heart rate when a person stands up and can lead to exhaustion and dizziness. "You know how people say, 'Oh, I'm so fatigued.' I've never used those words. I don't even like to speak in those terms, but I really was like that," Porziņģis said ahead of last season. "At that time, I could just lay on the couch and be a house cat."Porziņģis has been away from Warriors since SeptemberOver the last three seasons with the Celtics, Atlanta Hawks and Warriors, Porziņģis has only played 74 games. He has been away from the Warriors since late September and released a previous statement in mid-October shutting down rumors that he had been diagnosed with HIV or AIDS. At that point, the Warriors said Porziņģis would be out indefinitely. "Hello people, I'm working with doctors and experts to figure out how to be fully back to good health asap. Honestly, I'm getting better and better. I just have to stay patient, and I believe I'll be feeling great again soon," Porziņģis wrote. "It has definitely been frustrating dealing with some health stuff that you can't exactly pinpoint, on top of injuries throughout my career, so it has added up for sure, but we will get through it. Health is wealth. Thank you for all the support."
The Warriors hoped that Porziņģis would play a big role this season as a floor-spacing big, especially while Jimmy Butler (torn ACL) and Moses Moody (torn patellar tendon) remain sidelined. Instead, it seems more likely that he will never play for the franchise again. The Warriors have reportedly been trying to trade Porziņģis to use his $20 million cap figure, as explained by CBS Sports' Sam Quinn:While he would not have trade value as a player given his health status, he is essentially an expiring contract with only that small $3 million guarantee on the books for next season. That could potentially make him valuable to a team looking to move off of longer-term money, or the Warriors could entice another team into a trade using draft picks with Porziņģis serving only as the matching salary.
        
            
                Kristaps Porziņģis trade destinations: Three viable moves the Warriors could make to improve their roster
                
                    Sam Quinn                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Despite Porziņģis' absence, the Warriors are off to a 6-3 start, putting them in seventh place in the extremely crowded Western Conference standings. Rookie big man Yaxel Lendeborg has stepped up in Porziņģis' place and provided a major boost on both ends of the floor. 
Through nine games, Lendeborg is averaging 21 points, 7.1 rebounds, 4.1 assists and 1.1 steals while shooting 49.2% from the field, including 39.6% from 3-point range.

title: Antonio Brown avoids jail time, receives punishment after plea deal in Miami shooting - CBS Sports
description: The former NFL star was accused of opening fire at a man last year
body:
The former NFL star was accused of opening fire at a man last year
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 6, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:03 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Former NFL wide receiver Antonio Brown will not serve jail time after he pleaded guilty Friday to a lesser charge stemming from a shooting incident at a boxing event in Miami last year. The Super Bowl-winning ex-player was originally sought on one charge of attempted murder in May 2025 after a fight allegedly took place between Brown and several other individuals shortly after a celebrity boxing event. Brown pleaded guilty this week to aggravated assault with a firearm and received three years of probation. Brown will undergo a mandatory psychological evaluation and may have to attend weekly counseling if mandated by a judge."My client was facing 30 years in prison with a 20-year minimum mandatory, and he was given an offer he just couldn't refuse," Brown's defense attorney, Mark Eiglarsh, told reporters. "Probation was too good to turn down, and we're both very excited about the outcome."
Videos from the altercation circulated on social media, as did pictures of Brown in handcuffs. Brown later posted on social media claiming he was jumped by people trying to take his jewelry. "Regarding the boxing event that happened last night," Brown wrote at the time. "I was jumped by multiple individuals who tried to steal my jewelry and cause physical harm to me. Contrary to some video circulating, Police temporarily detained me until they received my side of the story and then released me. I WENT HOME THAT NIGHT AND WAS NOT ARRESTED."I will be talking to my legal council [sic] and attorneys on pressing charges on the individuals that jumped me. I will keep you all posted step-by-step on the process. Thank you for the support and love."
Brown last played in the NFL for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the 2021 season when he stormed off the field shirtless after getting into a heated argument with then-coach Bruce Arians.He said he was returning to the league to play for the Baltimore Ravens in 2023, but nothing materialized. In June 2024, Brown filed for bankruptcy, blaming lawsuits and others for his financial misfortunes.Five years prior to filing, Brown served an eight-game suspension for violating the league's personal conduct policy as a result of sexual and personal misconduct allegations levied against him.
From 2010-18 with the Pittsburgh Steelers, Brown was named to the Pro Bowl seven times and was a four-time All-Pro. He played for the New England Patriots for one game in 2019 before he was cut for sending threatening text messages to a woman. He spent his final two seasons with the Buccaneers.

title: Knicks defend Taylor Swift after Tyler Kolek, Deuce McBride question her fandom - CBS Sports
description: The organization was compelled to respond after two Knicks players were dismissive of Swift's fandom
body:
The organization was compelled to respond after two Knicks players were dismissive of Swift's fandom
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 6, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:12 pm ET

        The New York Knicks have released a statement supporting Taylor Swift's fandom after recent comments from reserve guards Tyler Kolek and Deuce McBride. "Taylor Swift has been a Knicks fan for many years, has a long history with Madison Square Garden, and we are incredibly appreciative of her support of the organization," a Knicks spokesperson said. Earlier this month, Kolek called Swift's fandom "a little performative" on an NBA 2K League video. Kolek and McBride were playing a game called "Deflected," where they have to compete in NBA 2K to avoid answering awkward questions. After McBride scored on the game, Kolek had to answer: "Who's the fakest celebrity fan you've seen sitting courtside in an NBA game?""At the Knicks games, I would say it's very performative," Kolek said. "Because they just want to be seen at the game; they're not necessarily fans. Maybe Taylor Swift?" "I would agree," McBride said."I don't know if I've seen her at any other games," Kolek said.
"Swifties not gonna like that answer," McBride replied. "No, I'm gonna get some hate from the Swifties," Kolek acknowledged. "I get she's got a lot going on, so she can't come all the time, but it's a little performative." 
This is not the first time Swift's Knicks fandom has been questioned. "She's not a Knicks fan. Get outta here, girl," broadcaster Monica McNutt said in June after Swift sat courtside during Game 4 of the 2026 NBA Finals, which the Knicks won with a historic 29-point comeback. McNutt later apologized for the comments. Swift was born and raised in Pennsylvania, but has been a Knicks fan since moving to New York over a decade ago. Here's an excerpt from an interview with Time Magazine in 2014:
You recently moved to New York. Are you a Knicks fan now?Yeah, totally.You realize they're not very good.I love them, though. Why does that matter? So you run into a bunch of different, interesting types of people at the Met Ball. I've gone the last four years. And the most normal people at that event, every single time, are Amar'e Stoudemire and his wife Alexis. I talk with them and hang with them every time I'm there. So I've always had this sort of love of the Knicks, just because Amar'e is so cool. And also I performed at the Knicks'—at Madison Square Garden's—Kids Talent Competition at halftime when I was 12 or 13. And ever since then I've had this kind of sparkly, magical opinion of Madison Square Garden and the Knicks, since they let me sing when I was a little kid. Swift and Kansas City Chiefs star Travis Kelce were married at Madison Square Garden during a lavish wedding in July.

title: Valparaiso stuns Purdue: Buzzer-beating 3-pointer in 2OT sends Boilermakers to first 0-2 start since 1976 - CBS Sports
description: Purdue entered Friday's game against Valparaiso as a 19.5-point favorite
body:
Purdue entered Friday's game against Valparaiso as a 19.5-point favorite
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 6, 2026
                            
                    at

                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Fox Broadcast
            
            

    
        Another major upset in college basketball headlined on Friday night in West Lafayette, Indiana, when Valparaiso handed Purdue a stunning 83-80 loss in double overtime. With the game tied at 80 in the final seconds, Valpo guard Justus McNair knocked down a corner 3-pointer as time expired to hand Purdue its second loss of the season.Valpo sent the game to double overtime after Rakim Chaney knocked down a 3-pointer at the buzzer to tie the game at 70. The Boilermakers led by as many as 15 points in the first half.The Boilermakers were 19.5-point favorites against Valparaiso and are now 0-2 for the first time since the 1976-77 season. Purdue is the latest high-major team to suffer a stunning loss during the opening week of the season. On opening night, Oklahoma lost to East Texas A&M as a 28.5-point favorite.
Purdue was riding a 23-game home winning streak during November. The loss to Valpo marked the first loss against a Missouri Valley Conference opponent at Mackey Arena since 1978, when Purdue lost to a Larry Bird-led Indiana State team.
The Boilermakers are in the midst of a major transition after Braden Smith, Trey Kaufman-Renn and Fletcher Loyer departed the program. That trio was among the most experienced in the sport and helped Purdue reach the Elite Eight in their final season together. Kaufman-Renn, of course, is playing his sixth season of college basketball with Kansas after being granted a motion for a preliminary injunction against the NCAA.

title: Brandon Aiyuk returns to 49ers offices to seek NFL reinstatement as $13 million problem looms - CBS Sports
description: The wide receiver says he is 100% healthy and filing for NFL reinstatement, though a $13 million financial disput
body:
The wide receiver says he is 100% healthy and filing for NFL reinstatement, though a $13 million financial dispute remains
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 6, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:37 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk returned to the team offices on Friday and has begun to take the necessary steps to file for reinstatement. Aiyuk recently hired agent Drew Rosenhaus to represent him, and the two addressed reporters ahead of their meeting with the team. The former Second Team All-Pro pass-catcher issued a short statement saying he's healthy and ready to go. "I'm feeling great, feeling healthy, been a long recovery process, long rehab process but I'm back to 100% and looking to get reinstated to the National Football League," Aiyuk said.
Aiyuk returning to Santa Clara was a big story on Friday. Well, big to everyone except 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan. He has since moved on from the Aiyuk drama and said he couldn't care less what happened during Friday's meeting. 
There are a few obstacles that Aiyuk will have to navigate before he can suit up again. Tom Pelissero of The Ringer reports that Aiyuk owes the 49ers about $13 million in bonus forfeiture. If you recall, the team signed Aiyuk to a four-year, $120 million extension in August of 2024, then voided about $27 million of salary guarantees in July the following year after he did not meet the requirements in his contract. Aiyuk was then placed on the reserve/left squad list. Pelissero reports that the NFL management council and the NFL Players Association are both working to find a resolution, although it may take some time. Additionally, the 49ers still own Aiyuk's rights. When he's reinstated by the league, the 49ers will have to trade or release him. San Francisco has failed to trade him in the past, meaning a release of his rights could be on the table after the $13 million problem is settled. 
This marks the beginning of the end to a strange saga that included a contract holdout, an injury, a desertion and a social media circus.What happened with Brandon Aiyuk?In 2023, Aiyuk had established himself as one of the best wide receivers in the NFL. He caught 75 passes for 1,342 yards and seven touchdowns as the 49ers made it all the way to Super Bowl LVIII. Aiyuk's 3.1 yards per route run that year ranked No. 3 behind Tyreek Hill and Nico Collins, and his 81.3% of receptions going for a first down or a touchdown ranked first in the NFL. Aiyuk joined Jerry Rice that year as the only players in franchise history to record seven 100-yard receiving games in a season. He was dynamic downfield, catching 14 of 20 passes thrown both outside the numbers and with 15+ air yards in 2023. It was the best rate (70%) of any player in the last four seasons (min. 20 targets), per CBS Sports Research. Aiyuk had one more year remaining on his rookie deal via the fifth-year option, but he wanted long-term security heading into 2024.  
Not long after the 49ers' Super Bowl loss to the Kansas City Chiefs, Aiyuk's girlfriend published an interesting TikTok. "This might have been the last day we touched foot on Levi's Stadium," she said, "because we might not be out here next year."However, 49ers general manager John Lynch said in March of 2024 that they were working on an extension with Aiyuk, and would not be trading him.
"Brandon's one that we think incredibly highly of, one of my favorite guys around our building," Lynch said, via the 49ers' official website. Things appeared to change as the offseason rolled on. Ahead of the 2024 NFL Draft, the 49ers began to explore a potential deal involving Aiyuk. The San Francisco Chronicle reported that the 49ers wanted a first-round pick for their top receiver. One NFL executive claimed, "they want too much." When the draft did roll around, the 49ers selected a wide receiver at No. 31 overall in Ricky Pearsall. Even after the addition of Pearsall, Lynch said on the "Pat McAfee Show," they were past trading Aiyuk or Deebo Samuel. 
"I'm doing everything in my power to keep our roster together," Lynch said. "That's my goal, and I don't question that. When you talk about guys like Brandon Aiyuk and Deebo, those are guys that we drafted, and we take a lot of pride in what they've become and who they've become. We couldn't be more proud of those guys. And so, during the course of drafts and offseasons, do conversations happen? Absolutely, they do. We're past that now. We're thrilled to add to that group."In June, the 49ers reported to mandatory minicamp. Aiyuk did not. He started talking about playing for other teams publicly, listing the Washington Commanders and Pittsburgh Steelers as potential landing spots."If not a Niners uniform, probably a Washington Commanders uniform," Aiyuk said during an appearance on "The Pivot" podcast. "If not a Washington Commanders uniform, probably Steelers uniform."
The next month, Aiyuk finally demanded a trade. Teams had reached out to the 49ers about Aiyuk, but were told San Francisco did not plan to trade him, per ESPN. Aiyuk did show up to training camp, but was "holding in" as he awaited a new contract. It got to the point where NFL Media reported that contract talks between Aiyuk and the 49ers had been stalled for quite some time, and it was more likely the star pass-catcher would be traded than find lucrative, long-term security in San Francisco.However, less than a month later, Aiyuk signed a four-year, $120 million extension with the 49ers. At $30 million per season, it tied the fifth-largest average annual value for a wide receiver contract at the time.
After sitting out offseason work and the preseason, Aiyuk started the 2024 campaign slowly. He failed to reach 50 yards receiving in each of his first four games before finally breaking out with 147 yards on eight catches in Week 5 against the Arizona Cardinals. He caught two passes for 37 yards the following week vs. the Seattle Seahawks, then tore his ACL in the Super Bowl rematch against the Chiefs in Week 7.Naturally, Aiyuk was forced to miss the remainder of the 2024 season, but questions started being raised about when he would return to the lineup in 2025. In November, The Athletic reported that the team had voided the $27 million of 2026 salary guarantees owed to Aiyuk in the summer after he failed to meet the obligations in his contract. The next month, Aiyuk was placed on the reserve/left team list. Shanahan said at the time that he hadn't seen Aiyuk "in forever" and that Aiyuk had been "extremely distant."Later that month, Aiyuk filmed himself driving 104 mph near the 49ers' stadium. The Santa Clara County District Attorney's Office issued a warrant for his arrest on a misdemeanor speeding charge -- which remains active to this day, by the way. 
Lynch publicly announced the 49ers would be taking calls on Aiyuk, but given that this was a receiver who seemingly quit on his team and his rehab, they didn't find a market. Still, San Francisco wasn't going to just release him. With Aiyuk still tied to the 49ers and unable to sign with another team, he began lashing out on social media. He called the 49ers "little-ass boys" during one rant posted to Instagram, and called the organization "stupid" for paying him."They mad 'cause they stupid," Aiyuk said. "They dumb. They mad that they paid me $50 million in eight months and then voided my guarantees for 2027. And I'm about to be on a new team in 2027. They mad at themselves for real. They acting like they mad at me, but they stupid ass mad at themselves."
Aiyuk started pretending as if he were close to signing with the Commanders and reuniting with his college quarterback in Jayden Daniels. In numerous videos, he donned Commanders gear and even claimed he bought a house in Ashburn -- where Washington's practice facility is located. However, Aiyuk had not applied for reinstatement and still had his rights owned by the 49ers. He missed the entire 2025 season, but has now shifted his focus. Aiyuk is finally playing ball and taking the necessary steps to finalize a divorce.

title: Kansas City Current and Angel City FC bring high scoring squads to quarterfinal action - CBS Sports
description: Kansas City Current host Angel City in the NWSL quarterfinals
body:
Kansas City Current host Angel City in the NWSL quarterfinals
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 6, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:08 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        When two of the NWSL's highest-scoring teams meet in a playoff game, you can expect fireworks. The Kansas City Current will host Angel City FC at CPKC Stadium on Saturday at 12 p.m. ET on CBS,  and the two sides are peaking at the right time as the postseason begins, with both clubs finishing the regular season with 54 goals scored.Kansas City have a 32-game home unbeaten streak that dates back to 2024, making the riverfront home a place where visiting teams typically lose. Angel City return to the playoffs for the first time since 2023 on a 10-game unbeaten run, and are equally relentless on the road. Angel City won the first regular-season meeting between them at BMO Stadium, 2-1, back in May, while the rematch in August ended in a 1-1 draw in Kansas City.Both teams took different paths to reach the playoffs and match up well on paper, but something has to give, and the winner advances to the semifinals.Here's everything you need to know about the big game on CBS:Kansas City playoff returnThe 2025 NWSL Shield winners had a tough start to the season. After the team was bounced out of the 2025 playoffs in the opening round, Vlatko Andonovski moved to an executive role while the club brought in Chris Armas as new head coach. Two-time Golden Boot winner Temwa Chawinga started the 2026 season on the injury report, and the club suffered multiple player departures, including Bia Zaneratto and Claire Hutton.\The early results were rough, with zero wins in the opening four games of the season, and players either not gelling together or occupying similar spaces or even running into each other. They maneuvered the first quarter of the schedule closer to the bottom half of the league table than the playoff line.
There was a doubling down of questions about Armas, his limited knowledge of the NWSL and women's pro soccer, and whether or not injuries or absences kept him from rolling out a complete lineup. But things finally shifted with the spring and, of course, the return of Chawinga.Midfielder Croix Bethune, who was acquired in preseason, grew into her role and set an NWSL single-season record with 11 assists, including six game-winning assists. Forward Haley Hopkins had a breakout season; after being traded to the club in 2025, she co-leads the team with Chawinga in goals (12) this year. The roster's 54 goals are split across 13 different players."I'd say that what's clear is that we've just come together. Is it the right time? It's just an important time of year to have most of your players healthy. We're at a good fitness level. The team has been together all year, but you have to go through things sometimes to, you know, see your best version. And sometimes it's adversity. And when does that come? I've always said that oftentimes teams experience that in a season, and we had a lot of it this year," Armas told CBS Sports.
"On the outside, they might just see we're not getting results, or they might ignore some of the performances for a long time. Things like XG, and like, we just had a process. We talk about sticking to it, but the team has been through a lot of change, a lot of injuries this year early on to key players, and all along I know whether a team believes it or not, we were finding different ways of doing things. Some of it was by design because I'm a new coach to the team. Some of it was finding different ways to score and different people to rely on, and different ways to attack and create chances. And even some of our high press and mid block, and some of it was different ways of doing things," Armas explained.All of the ups and downs and adjustments were ultimately seeds planted along the way, Armas also said. The playoffs are maybe just the time to harvest, but mostly it's about how the team is performing on a consistent basis now, and how that's reverberated throughout the locker room."I think that we've gotten to see some of that come to fruition throughout the season, but consistently right now, which then is the belief and confidence that comes, and that's contagious. It's contagious for Angel City. It's contagious for teams like Gotham and Washington, like some of these teams that have done really well. And it's been contagious for us ... So we're in a good moment, and it all resets because we play against another team in a good moment. But we like where we're at. We like who we are, and we're up for it," he said.
Angel City's remarkable second halfMaybe Angel City's executives cracked the code to a long season. If you're not doing well and there is still a ton of season left, maybe just go ahead and make the call. They made multiple. While big gambles don't always pay off, they are paying off right now for Angel City.First, the club parted ways with head coach Alexander Straus in June. After a three-game win streak to open the season, the club hit a massive speed bump and managed only one win over its next eight games. They then used the summer break to make another bold move, trading $850,000 in intraleague transfer funds to the Kansas City Current for forward Ally Sentnor.With Leif Gunnar Smerud as interim head coach, Sentnor's addition, and the return of Savy King to the backline, the club went on one of its best runs in club history. The group has one loss in its last 14 games and is on a 10-game unbeaten streak heading into the quarterfinals. They co-lead the regular season with Kansas City in goals scored (54), with as many different goal scorers (13) as their playoff opponent.
Sveindis Jonsdottir and Maiara Niehues each set club records for single-season goals, scoring 19 between them. But the defense has been just as essential to the surge in form. Goalkeeper Angelina Anderson posted 10 clean sheets, and fullbacks King and Evelyn Shores elevated their play, with Shores leading the team with eight assists."We are in a good place. We're gonna have to keep doing what we've been doing well, which is play the game and the situation in front of us. We have been able to go to very different games and game scenarios, and opponents and stadiums, and sort of managed to find a way to win, and done it with courage and with the attacking mindset," Smerud told CBS Sports."We scored a lot of goals. I think most in the league, together with Kansas. So it's to go out there and be us, and then of course be prepared for. It's a home playoff game for them, and they will certainly want to win it. But we have to be ready from the start. That's the main thing. And we can for sure go there and win this game. But it's not going to come for free," he said.
What's nextThe NWSL quarterfinals are underway; the winner of Kansas City Current vs. Angel City will face the winner of Gotham FC vs. Seattle Reign in the semifinals. The semifinal round of the NWSL playoffs will take place on Nov. 14 and 15.

title: Saint Louis star Robbie Avila granted preliminary injunction, will play Friday vs. rival Missouri - CBS Sports
description: Saint Louis looks like a top-25 team and the firm A-10 favorite with Avila in the fold, but the College Sports Co
body:
Saint Louis looks like a top-25 team and the firm A-10 favorite with Avila in the fold, but the College Sports Commission is currently blocking the reigning A-10 Player of the Year due to a roster-limit snafu.
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 6, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:00 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Saint Louis star big man Robbie Avila, the reigning A-10 Player of the Year, will return to the Billikens for a fifth year of eligibility after Missouri judge Jason Sengheiser granted Avila a preliminary injunction, just a day before SLU's enormous non-conference tilt against rival Missouri. Avila was expected to suit up and make his 2026-27 debut for Josh Schertz's club, but it hit a late snag Friday. The College Sports Commission is blocking Avila's return to the floor because adding a 16th player to SLU's roster would violate the roster limits imposed by the injunctive relief settlement in House v. NCAA. Sengheiser's decision drew some eyebrow raises because the court order ruled that the NCAA was not allowed to enforce its roster limits to block Avila from returning to Saint Louis' already-filled, 15-man roster. "While we take no position on Mr. Avila's eligibility, we cannot effectuate a state court order that requires us to violate the explicit terms of a federal injunctive relief settlement by giving Saint Louis University an additional roster slot," the CSC released in a statement. "Mr. Avila may be eligible to play college basketball this season, but there is no roster slot available for him at Saint Louis University." There are currently over 50 fifth-year seniors who are eligible and 16 who are not at the high-major ranks, according to Sports Illustrated's Kevin Sweeney. Avila's representation is expected to fight the CSC's ruling. If eligible, Avila's return is a massive boon for Saint Louis and college basketball. Dubbed Milk Chamberlain, Larry Nerd, Cream Abdul-Jabbar or Rob Wave, Avila has become one of the most recognizable names in the game. 
He can hoop, too. Avila averaged 12.8 points and shot 41% from 3-point range on 4.6 attempts for a Saint Louis offense that ranked second in the country in effective field goal percentage last season. Saint Louis started 24-1 last year, en route to earning an at-large bid and the No. 9 seed in the NCAA Tournament. It bulldozed Georgia, 102-77, in the first round before falling short to eventual champion Michigan in the Round of 32. It was Saint Louis' first NCAA Tournament win since 2014.
        
            
                Grading college basketball debuts: First impressions of LSU's Will Wade, UNC, top transfers, 5-star freshmen
                
                    Isaac Trotter                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
With Avila back in the fold, Saint Louis would have four starters back and two more key rotation players who hooped in the Big Dance. Expectations are extremely high, especially after Saint Louis' brass held off high-major poachers from Schertz, who is the hottest name in the coaching carousel. Avila may need a bit of time to knock off the rust in the early-going, but its wheels up for Saint Louis' 2026-27 long-term outlook. The Billikins are now the only team in America to retain three high-volume 40% 3-point shooters. Avila, Trey Green and Ishan Sharma combined to deposit 233 3-pointers last year. Bombs away.
But it's more than just 3s that makes Saint Louis' offense so hard to guard. The threat of the aerial assault opens up the paint. When Avila was on the floor, Saint Louis shot a whopping 63% at the rim. The layup is the most efficient shot in basketball, and nearly half (45% to be exact) of Saint Louis' shots came at the rim thanks to Avila's ability to draw shot-blockers away from the basket and make reads as a passer.Saint Louis looks like a top-25 team if it all clicks and the firm A-10 favorite if Avila can play. The market for two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal, far and away the offseason's best free agent, is already hot, according to the New York Post. Talks are underway, however, and his market is moving.Skubal is expected to sign a record contract at least in total value, and possibly in average annual value. We ranked Sato as the fourth-best free agent available this offseason, and the best available position player. Cadeau is a wizard playmaker who mixes speed, power and creativity. In an ideal world, Cadeau would love to finish a game with 12 assists rather than 20 points, but new Michigan head coach Mike Boynton Jr. may need him to score more than ever before. That's easier said than done because Demary is an elite point-of-attack defender. Demary is all of 6-foot-5 who takes it personally if anyone works him for a bucket. The team with the best point guard play will win this game, but it's as close to a draw on paper.Portal bigs: UConn and Michigan had to replace a combined five NBA players who all played in the frontcourt. UConn spent big in the portal for Seton Hall transfer Na'jai Hines, who is a total freak. Michigan did the same with Cincinnati transfer Moustapha Thiam, who is expected to suit up in this one after missing the opener against Oakland with an illness. Bigs from the portal always take a little time to fully coalesce for their new teams, but UConn and Michigan don't have time to wait. Thiam and Hines need to be immediate difference-makers. 
Specifically, keep an eye on when UConn aggressively hard-hedges Michigan's ball screens. Hines can be a bit foul-prone when he's flying out to try and be disruptive. Those avoidable fouls drove Dan Hurley up a wall in the preseason and earned Hines plenty of time on the pine. Conversely, that coverage forces the ball out of Cadeau's hands and into Thiam's hands. The 7-foot-2 big fella has to make good decisions if Michigan wants to find good shots, but he's not a great passer (yet). Friday's test should be enlightening on both sides of the aisle.Preseason hints: Some over-index on preseason results. Others completely ignore them. The truth is likely more in the middle. In the preseason, UConn's defense looked way ahead of schedule. It put Purdue in clamps for long stretches. Hurley has grown men, positional size and at least one elite defender at every single level. Meanwhile, Michigan doesn't look super connected on defense yet. We already knew Michigan's defense was not going to be on the level of the 2025-26 squad's special group. The question is whether this UM squad is a top-25 or top-50 unit. Cadeau and Demary are a draw at point guard. Snipers like Trey McKenney and Braylon Mullins are pretty similar. On and on we go. The difference is the bench. UConn can bring a potential first-round pick off the bench in linebacker Colben Landrew. Michigan planned to have something similar, but five-star freshman Brandon McCoy Jr. blew out his knee on the Wolverines' international tour. UConn is the deeper team and looks ahead of schedule on both ends of the floor. Michigan's defense isn't airtight, and I also struggle to envision how the Wolverines create good shots if Cadeau ever gets into foul trouble.

But two whole possessions feels a bit rich for a game where the top-shelf talent is basically even on both sides. UConn can out-physical a lot of teams, but not Michigan. Asking him to be anything more than that might be problematic, even if his pass protection won't be too rough. Last year at UConn he connected with Skyler Bell on a ton of quick throws, but not necessarily all short throws, for huge numbers. My best guess is that the Ravens scheme up a slew of targets to Zay Flowers against the Jaguars' zone-heavy defense with the hope he breaks a couple of plays for big yardage. The Jaguars happen to rank bottom-five in both yards per attempt and average depth of throw allowed to receivers on throws under 2.5 seconds, but it's not like they've been crushed on quick passes -- Darius Cooper had a long touchdown against a coverage bust and Keenan Allen had a lot of quick-game volume to help push their numbers to decent totals.         This week in the NFL, the Cincinnati Bengals and Atlanta Falcons will do battle in Madrid, the Green Bay Packers will look to spoil Rob Gronkowski's Patriots Hall of Fame induction in New England, and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers attempt to make up ground in the NFC South against the surging Chicago Bears.Injuries are mounting across the league as we cross the halfway point of the 2026 season, and that includes at quarterback. Shedeur Sanders will make his first start of the season for the Cleveland Browns in place of Deshaun Watson as they take on the New Orleans Saints, Drew Lock replaces Sam Darnold in the lineup for the Seattle Seahawks, and Carson Wentz will try to make the most of his opportunity against the Buffalo Bills with Kyler Murray sidelined by a hamstring injury. Another notable injury storyline is with new Seahawks offensive guard Quenton Nelson. Just one week after trading a third-round pick and future fifth-round pick to the Indianapolis Colts for the eight-time Pro Bowl left guard, head coach Mike Macdonald told reporters that Nelson needs a minor knee procedure. NFL Media reports it's to clean out cartilage, as fragments have been causing an issue. Seattle says Nelson will avoid injured reserve right now, and is week-to-week. That means the Seahawks offensive line will likely revert to their old format, with Grey Zabel at left guard and Anthony Bradford at right guard.  Below, we will break down the final injury reports for all teams set to play on Sunday, beginning with our international game in Spain.

title: Is Drew Mestemaker really QB1? A troubling trend and lessons from Caleb Williams, Trevor Lawrence - CBS Sports

body:
The Oklahoma State QB has become a popular QB1 choice, but his mistakes under pressure offer a warning – and some fascinating historical comparisons.
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 6, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:16 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Caleb Williams. Trevor Lawrence. Drew Mestemaker.Two former No. 1 overall picks and probably the hottest name in the 2027 NFL Draft all share a troubling distinction: Over the last decade-plus, only Williams and Lawrence had higher turnover-worthy-play rates under pressure in their final college seasons than Mestemaker has this year.But there's a catch. For Williams and Lawrence, those numbers were one-year blips after considerably better performances earlier in their college careers. For Mestemaker, the mistakes have followed him from North Texas to Oklahoma State … and they've gotten worse.
None of that means Mestemaker can't be the first quarterback selected in the 2027 NFL Draft. He's put himself squarely in the QB1 conversation, and for good reason. I have Miami's Darian Mensah just ahead of him, but there's a whole lot to like about Mestemaker's game. NFL teams will also have to answer an important question before investing a high first-round pick in him: What happens when defenses take away the easy throws and force him to make decisions under pressure?
Why Mestemaker belongs in the QB1 conversationThere's plenty to like about the Oklahoma State quarterback, who spent last season at North Texas. For starters, Mestemaker looks the part. He has a strong arm, throws with anticipation and will get through his reads. He's comfortable attacking all three levels, manipulates defenders with his eyes and has the patience to stand in the pocket, reset his feet and deliver fastballs into tight windows.
He has plenty of NFL-caliber throws on tape, especially on intermediate routes where he has to throw receivers open. It's easy to see why he's become a popular QB1 choice. But there are also stretches where he tries to do too much, and that's where the evaluation gets more complicated.The concern isn't just this seasonThrough Week 9 of 2026, Mestemaker has seven turnover-worthy plays on 54 dropbacks when he was pressured, according to PFF. That's a 13.0% rate, more than double the 5.8% median for the first-round quarterbacks in our historical comparison.
(A turnover-worthy play isn't just an interception. It can be a dangerous throw that a defender drops or another mistake that puts the football at risk. And while the number itself doesn't tell us everything, it helps identify decisions that might otherwise get lost in the box score.)Williams and Lawrence were the only first-rounders we looked at with higher rates in their final college seasons, but both had been considerably better the previous year. Williams went from 0.9% in 2022 to 15.3% in 2023, while Lawrence jumped from 1.6% in 2019 to 13.2% in 2020.Turnover-worthy play percentage and yards per attempt when pressuredQBSeasonTWP %YPACaleb Williams202315.3%6.8Trevor Lawrence202013.2%8.3Drew Mestemaker2026*13.0%4.5Jordan Love201910.9%2.8Sam Darnold201710.5%11.0Josh Allen20178.9%6.7Patrick Mahomes20168.5%9.4* 2026 season through Week 9. Source: PFFLook at Williams and Lawrence now. Both had bumpy starts to their NFL careers, and both are now two of the NFL's best quarterbacks. It's a pretty good reminder that A.) landing in the right situation is probably the most important factor in a young QB's development, and B.) troubling college numbers don't mean you're destined to fail at the next level.Mestemaker's struggles have followed him from North Texas to Oklahoma State. His turnover-worthy-play rate was 8.3% under pressure in 2025 before climbing to 13% so far this season. Over that span, he's put the ball in harm's way 13 times in 126 such situations. That's a 10.3% rate, and it's something NFL evaluators will have to consider.Of course, there's recent precedent for NFL teams looking past troubling numbers. I wrote last November about Ty Simpson's historically poor deep-ball accuracy, and we later learned just how much injuries had affected his play. The Rams still took him 13th overall in April, betting on everything else he did well.Here's what makes it even more interesting: Mestemaker has gotten much better at avoiding sacks, but he's also making more dangerous throws. Last season, he was sacked on roughly 21% of plays when pressured. That number is down to 11% this year, but while he's taking fewer sacks, he's also averaging a full yard less per pass attempt in those situations (5.6 to 4.5).The tape provides more clues. Mestemaker generally shows good footwork and accuracy when he has time, and he's capable of working beyond his first read. But there are also moments when he forces throws into coverage instead of taking the easier completion underneath, or when his accuracy suffers because he doesn't get his feet set.These aren't all necessarily mistakes caused by pressure, but they point to a similar concern: knowing when to challenge a defense and when to take what it's giving you.What Mahomes, Allen, Love and Darnold can tell usThe good news for Mestemaker is that other really talented quarterbacks have entered the NFL with concerns about their decision-making under pressure. A lot of them have gone on to be really good. Of course, not everyone develops the same way.Let's start with Patrick Mahomes. In his final season at Texas Tech, he had an 8.5% turnover-worthy-play rate when pressured, but he also averaged 9.4 yards per attempt and generated 14 big-time throws. Mestemaker, by comparison, has averaged just 4.5 YPA this season, with three big-time throws against seven turnover-worthy plays.Mahomes took risks, but he was also creating considerably more positive plays when things broke down. That's an important distinction because making dangerous throws is one thing; consistently making spectacular plays to offset those mistakes is another.Jordan Love offers a different lesson. His final season at Utah State was a mess compared with his outstanding 2018 campaign. He went from 32 touchdowns and six interceptions to 20 touchdowns and 17 picks, and his turnover-worthy-play rate under pressure jumped from 3.4% to 10.9%.Love averaged just 2.8 yards per attempt when pressured in 2019, even worse than Mestemaker this season. Green Bay still took him in the first round, betting on his physical talent and development. That patience paid off, a reminder that a concerning college season doesn't have to define a quarterback's NFL career.Then there's Josh Allen, who happens to be Mestemaker's favorite quarterback. Allen inspired him to wear No. 17, and Mestemaker has talked about relating to Allen's unconventional football journey.Allen's final college season wasn't nearly as productive as the one before. His passing yards fell from 3,203 to 1,812, his yards per attempt dropped from 8.6 to 6.7, and he completed just 56.3% of his passes. His turnover-worthy-play rate under pressure was 8.9%, yet Buffalo took him seventh overall because his physical tools were impossible to ignore.Allen developed into JOSH ALLEN. While Mestemaker's best ball is likely in front of him too, it's unfair to expect anyone to make the leap Allen made once he arrived in the league.Sam Darnold provides another example. His turnover-worthy-play rate under pressure was 10.5% in his final season at USC, but he also averaged 11.0 yards per attempt in those situations. Like Mahomes, he took chances, but he also made big plays when things broke down.The point isn't that Mestemaker will become the next Mahomes, Allen, Love or Darnold. It's that quarterbacks can overcome weaknesses, but the risks have to be weighed against what they do well and what they're capable of becoming.So where does that leave Mestemaker?I still like Mestemaker a lot and there's every reason to believe he could be the first quarterback taken in either this draft or in 2028, should he decide to stay in school another year. But the mistakes under pressure are real, and they're going to be a part of his evaluation.There's also time for him to get better, likely even a lot better. Remember, Mestemaker never started a varsity game at quarterback in high school; he was primarily a punter and safety before walking on at North Texas. He's already improved at avoiding sacks, and the next step is making smarter decisions when defenses disrupt his timing. Mestemaker has the talent to be the first quarterback selected whenever he enters the draft. But making NFL throws and making NFL decisions aren't the same thing. And how much he improves his decision-making under pressure could ultimately determine just how early he'll hear his name called.
